verdict: APPROVE the one-line libSystem fix and the candidate-006 RAM root for a bounded RAM-only runtime test, once the concrete packet bindings are reviewed. The library differs from the RAM's current libSystem (432c7369) only in where vm_page_size comes from: libdyld's correctly initialised global instead of a stale local 4096. That is, however, a process-wide behaviour change (W1/W2) that only a run can qualify.

library.provenance: Patch: deletes exactly 'vm_size_t vm_page_size = 4096;' from src/Libraries/libSystem/stub/pd_libSystem_compat.c. Derivation pzjiy6qk vs vzr04lys (the producer of jll17vb2, whose libSystem.B.dylib is 432c7369, byte-equal to the RAM baseline file): identical inputDrvs; the only new input source is the patch (store copy f51b1092); env changes are only name/pname/out/patches. The output binary hashes to 8ff49e0c.
library.binary_diff: Load-command names and dylibs used are unchanged (libdyld is the only LC_REEXPORT_DYLIB). Defined symbols: _vm_page_size (local __DATA,__data at 0x2b6800) is removed; an indirect entry '_vm_page_size (for _vm_page_size)' is added. Undefined: only _vm_page_size (from libdyld) is added. Export trie: still 2370 entries; exactly one change, '_vm_page_size' becomes '[re-export] _vm_page_size (from libdyld)'.
library.abi: The new library imports 49 symbols, all from libdyld (old 48 plus _vm_page_size). Every one is exported by the retained /usr/lib/system/libdyld.dylib 428e224e (unchanged in RAM 006).
library.canonical_value: libdyld 428e224e defines and exports _vm_page_size/_vm_page_mask/_vm_page_shift (__DATA,__common) and _mach_init. In _mach_init the stores at 0x5eda0 (shift), 0x5edbc (size) and 0x5edcc (mask) implement libsystem_kernel/mach/mach_init.c: vm_page_shift from USER_PAGE_SHIFT_64, vm_page_size = 1 << shift, vm_page_mask = size - 1. The attempt-003 probe read mask 16383 and shift 14 from these same globals, so libdyld's vm_page_size is 16384, consistent with getpagesize, sysconf and host_page_size.

runtime_expectations_and_risks.text: 57 libSystem functions read vm_page_size through the GOT slot (0x2981C8) now bound to libdyld. They include malloc (_create_scalable_szone, _mvm_allocate_pages, _mvm_deallocate_pages, _mvm_protect, large-entry paths, valloc/memalign), pthread (_pthread_allocate, guardsize, wqthread setup), dispatch heaps and I/O, os_alloc, mach_msg_server and asl. Before, all saw 4096; now all see 16384 in every process. This matches Apple's 16K arm64 behaviour, but it has never run here.

Expected improvement: the 'can't mvm_protect(0) region for postlude guard page' warnings should disappear because guard pages become page-aligned. Consequence: guard pages may now actually be armed, so a latent heap overrun in PureDarwin userland that used to be silent could fault. A crash in that case is a finding to analyse, not proof the fix is wrong.

Probe qualification: the page-probe JSON should report vm_page_size 16384 with mask 16383 and shift 14, and the vm_protect/mprotect observations may change. The return test (shell, compositor, client, statuses, footer) must still complete; compare against attempt 003/005 behaviour.
